full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 224

Mou Mei (Tianjin) Image Technology Co., Ltd. v. Henan Mou Lu Bee Industry Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of the right to disseminate works through information network

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 15, 2023)

Keywords: civil litigation; infringement of the right to disseminate works through information network; ownership; burden of proof

Ruling Gist

Where ownership of copyright is disputed, the copyright ownership of a work shall not be determined solely on the basis of a watermark or a rights statement. The party claiming copyright shall provide further evidence; otherwise, it shall bear adverse legal consequences.

Basic Facts

Non-party Company G* authorized Mou Mei (Tianjin) Image Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mou Mei Image Company) to display, sell, and license others to use its "getty Images" brand images within China, and Mou Mei Image Company was entitled to initiate infringement lawsuits in its own name. Mou Mei Image Company discovered that Henan Mou Lu Bee Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mou Lu Bee Company) had used four of the above brand images without permission. Mou Mei Image Company thus filed a lawsuit claiming copyright infringement, seeking an order that Mou Lu Bee Company compensate for economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights enforcement. In support of its claims, Mou Mei Image Company submitted an authorization confirmation letter issued by Company G* and a website rights statement, among other evidence. The disputed images bore a watermark of "getty Images®". Mou Lu Bee Company argued in its defense that the watermark on the images bore a trademark registration mark "®" in the upper right corner, which does not indicate the author's identity as a creator; below the watermark, the photographer's name and other brand names appeared, indicating that the copyright in the images belonged to the photographer, not to Mou Mei Image Company or Company G*. Mou Lu Bee Company also inquired about the ownership of the images via email with Company G* and received a reply that the images were submitted by a photographer, that the company sold them in its own name and paid royalties to the photographer, but the photographer retained the copyright in the images. Based on this reply, Mou Lu Bee Company contended that since the photographer retained the copyright, neither Company G* nor Mou Mei Image Company held copyright in the images, and Mou Mei Image Company's claims should be dismissed.

Judgment

The Tianjin No. 3 Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment ( (2019) Jin 03 Zhi Min Chu No. 73 ) on September 17, 2019, ordering Mou Lu Bee Company to pay Mou Mei Image Company RMB 8,000 in total for economic losses and reasonable expenses; and dismissing the other claims of Mou Mei Image Company. Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Mou Lu Bee Company appealed. The Tianjin High People's Court rendered a civil judgment ( (2020) Jin Min Zhong No. 311 ) on July 16, 2020, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Still dissatisfied, Mou Lu Bee Company applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. The Supreme People's Court decided to retry the case and rendered a civil judgment ( (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 355 ) on December 20, 2021, reversing the first- and second-instance judgments and dismissing all claims of Mou Mei Image Company.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held that the disputed images bore not only a "getty Images®" watermark but also the photographer's name and other brand names; moreover, the trademark registration mark "®" immediately followed "getty Images". Therefore, the copyright in the images could not be determined to belong to Company G* solely on the basis of this watermark. In addition, Mou Mei Image Company submitted an authorization confirmation letter and a website rights statement issued by Company G*. However, the confirmation letter could only prove the fact that Company G* had granted authorization to Mou Mei Image Company; it was not evidence that Company G* held copyright in the images. The rights statement is a unilateral declaration, and without corroboration by other evidence, copyright ownership cannot be determined solely on its basis. Under such circumstances, Mou Mei Image Company should have further bore the burden of proving that Company G* owned the copyright in the images, but it failed to do so. On the contrary, according to counter-evidence submitted by Mou Lu Bee Company, including a reply email from Company G*, Company G* confirmed that the photographer who submitted the images still retained the copyright in the images. Therefore, Mou Mei Image Company's claim that Company G* owned the copyright in the images could not be sustained, and the related claims it made in this case should not be supported.

Relevant Legal Provisions

1. Article 12 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2020) (this case applied Article 11 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2010).

2. Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Copyright (amended in 2020).

3. Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2022) (this case applied Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2020).
